name: Production Incident Response Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any production incident response task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any production incident response task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any production incident response bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Check that production incident response terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
3. Document any non-obvious production incident response decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. Validate production incident response outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to production incident response (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Prefer explicit, readable production incident response solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen production incident response approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. When production incident response decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Keep production incident response outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
10. When multiple production incident response strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
11. Before starting production incident response work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
12. State assumptions about production incident response explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic production incident response advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of production incident response correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated production incident response concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop production incident response edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for production incident response, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
